items.title: Gluing ring maps given at finitely many maximal ideals whose kernels and cokernels are killed locally
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the tame symbol
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma reconstructs a single ring map phi : A -> B from finitely many local ring maps phi_i : A_{m_i} -> B_i at pairwise distinct maximal ideals, with the requirement that the kernel and cokernel of phi are killed by a power of the intersection m_1 cap ... cap m_r, and it asks that finiteness, injectivity or surjectivity of all phi_i pass to phi (statement lines 527-540). The non-formal step is the reduction: the product A' = prod A_i satisfies IA' = prod m_i A_i and A -> A' is flat with A/I isomorphic to A'/IA', which is exactly what allows more-algebra-lemma-application-formal-glueing to be invoked and then more-algebra-remark-formal-glueing-algebras to put an A-algebra structure on the glued module (proof lines 546-555). The last observation, that Ker(phi)_{m_i} and Coker(phi)_{m_i} compute the local kernels and cokernels, is what converts the local hypotheses into the global statement. The claim is H2: short and citation-driven, but with one genuine reduction specific to the finitely many maximal ideals.
